rounds.text: Coastal Corporation Ltd trades at a compelling discount to its peers across multiple valuation metrics, offering a P/E ratio of 12.52x against a sector benchmark of 23.11x [E6], alongside an attractive EV/EBITDA of 8.76x compared to the sector benchmark of 14.52x [E11]. The business demonstrates tangible top-line momentum, highlighted by a compounded sales growth rate of 27% over the last 3 years [E16] and a trailing twelve-month profit growth surge of 83% [E21]. Furthermore, the company is trading at an accessible price-to-book ratio of 1.10x on a book value of ₹ 45.0 [E2], well below the sector benchmark P/B of 3.64x [E7]. This fundamental execution is supported by constructive technical and institutional signals, including positive institutional money flow [E43], a position above the 200-day moving average [E49], and an insider promoter holding increase to 42.31% [E40]. Conceded: [E37], [E44].

Coastal Corporation Ltd trades at a rich valuation that is completely disconnected from its underlying operational reality, carrying a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 23 per share against a market price of Rs 49.5, leaving a severe margin of safety of -115.5% [E44, E45]. The company's profitability and capital returns lag significantly behind sector benchmarks, with a dismal ROA of 3.14%, ROE of 9.4%, and ROCE of 9.06% [E8, E9, E10], alongside a 3-year median ROE of just 3% [E27]. Operational efficiency is deeply concerning as cash conversion has turned negative to -0.93x with operating cash flow plunging to Rs -13 Cr and free cash flow dropping to Rs -4 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, leverage risk is pronounced with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.02x as borrowings escalated to Rs 306 Cr, compounded by a low interest coverage ratio, stagnant quarterly operating margins at 0% in Mar 2026, and substantial contingent liabilities of Rs 133 Cr [E37, E38, E60, E62]. Conceded: [E16] and [E21].

The bear's invocation of the DCF intrinsic value at Rs 23 [E44] ignores the market's clear validation through a robust 35% compounded share price growth over 1 year [E24] and a strong twelve-month price return of 33.5% [E51]. While the bear points to low capital returns [E8, E9, E10], it overlooks that the company trades at an attractive P/E of 12.52x against a sector benchmark of 23.11x [E6], as well as a favourable EV/EBITDA of 8.76x compared to its sector benchmark of 14.52x [E11]. The alarm raised over cash flows [E33, E34, E35] ignores the dramatic operational turnaround seen in trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 83% [E21] and a 3-year compounded sales growth of 27% [E16]. Conceded: [E37, E60, E62]. Furthermore, institutional sentiment is actively backing the growth story with positive institutional money flow [E43] and domestic institutions increasing their stake to 1.03% from 0.00% [E42], all while the stock trades confidently above its 200-day moving average [E49, E68].
